items.text:
**Yes—this narrow repair completion is acceptable.** I found no conflicting interruption, debit-timing or fixed-ability rule in the reviewed equipment repair clauses, expedition FL-18 or the linked equipment review receipts.

**Source-backed:** [Equipment §Repair](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/9fd32abe010b768119ceae31b837340d431a4a9a/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/EQUIPMENT_ACQUISITION_PLAYTEST.md#L205) and [FL-18](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/9fd32abe010b768119ceae31b837340d431a4a9a/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/expedition/EXPEDITION_PLAYER_BOOK.md#L354) establish:

- Relevant trained tools and real compatible materials.
- Materials worth 25% of the applicable baseline: **12 gp 5 sp** here.
- `max(1 hour, maximum HP / 10 hours)`: **one active hour** here.
- **DC 10 tool task**, with Core natural shifts/degrees collapsed to binary.
- Success restores the existing maximum, **5 HP**; failure spends materials and labor.
- A zero-HP target remains eligible when its main body is recoverable.

**Task-specific fixture binding:** trained Carpenter’s tools proficiency, a separate usable toolkit, recoverable wooden case and intact implements establish a coherent repair method. **DEX + PB once** is an acceptable explicitly authored ability assignment for this physical task. The source leaves the “appropriate” tool task open; this does not establish DEX as the universal carpentry ability or grant a manufacturing trade.

**Agree to these NEW provisional lifecycle completions:**

| Event | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Schedule | Reserve one finite compatible allotment and the target’s repair claim. |
| First positive eligible labor | Consume the whole allotment once. No automatic purchase or second charge. |
| Pause/incapacity | Retain earned labor; resume explicitly after revalidation. |
| Full labor earned | Resolve the required check after the established automatic boundary sequence, using conditions then operative. |
| Incapable at that point | Persist fully worked `AwaitingCheck`; no RNG, additional labor or new labor window required. |
| Cancel before work | Release unspent material and target reservations. |
| Cancel after work | No refund. Close the attempt; a new attempt starts with fresh materials and zero labor credit. |
| Success/failure | Settle once and release the repair claim. Preserve all unrelated incident restrictions. |

Keep these implementation distinctions:

- **Target validity differs from tool usability.** A Broken target can be repaired; the separate repair toolkit must remain functional and appropriate.
- **Labor alone restores no HP.** Restoration occurs only with successful check resolution. Failure supplies no partial restoration.
- At resume/check, revalidate the same target, recoverable body, repair scope, toolkit, qualifications and access. An absent body or missing implements cannot be recreated by the recorded expenditure.
- `AwaitingCheck` preserves the target claim against overlapping repairs, but does not reserve additional worker hours. When eligible at ordinary completion, resolve immediately; it is not an elective opportunity to postpone the roll for better modifiers.
- Retain the existing pending-tactical-choice barrier for any repair check that would consume RNG.
- Structural success changes HP/Broken functionality only. Miscalibration, fouling, lost-log obligations, ownership and other history remain intact.

This remains a **repair-specific completion**. It does not change manufacturing’s phase-loss procedure or introduce crafting quality, mishaps or trade XP into repair.

I adopt77b4ae6d access distinctions. The selected repair explicitly uses the same affected physical workbench, with compatible case-repair setup/intact implements; not merely same plot. StartToolRepair is immediate active work instruction (no separate queued scheduling command); validated start/resume pauses conflicting primary-tool research atomically. Paused/AwaitingCheck releases productive exclusivity while retaining repair claim, and final explicit check reacquires access without hours. A source nuance surfaced: schema16's shared ResearchAccess gated both research AND simple copying on the broken Alchemy kit. Ordinary legible-formula copying only requires actual writing supplies/time; it does not appear to use Alchemist's supplies. I propose correct this before repair qualification: broken/actively-repaired Alchemy kit gates only the selected primary-tool-using research task, not ordinary text copying; spill still gates copying at the actual selected bench. Active repair pauses research using its target, not a different worker copying with independent writing supplies; same worker cannot do both simultaneously and requires explicit pause. This seems source fidelity, not a new copying gameplay cost. Please confirm.

items.text:
**Confirmed: this is a source-fidelity correction, not a new copying cost.**

The [copying clause](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/9fd32abe010b768119ceae31b837340d431a4a9a/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CRAFTING_HARVEST_PLAYTEST.md#L174) requires a legible, legitimately accessible formula, one active hour and writing supplies. It supplies no Alchemist’s-kit prerequisite.

Separate eligibility by procedure:

- **Selected research:** requires its explicitly bound primary toolkit; Broken or active repair can block it.
- **Ordinary copying:** requires its actual reading/writing capability, formula access, supplies and work access. The Alchemy kit’s condition is irrelevant.
- **Spill:** blocks copying when copying actually uses that affected bench.
- **Repair preemption:** pauses research using the repaired target. It does not automatically pause another worker’s independent copying.
- **Same worker:** copying must be explicitly paused before incompatible repair begins. A rejected repair start must leave copying unchanged.

One qualification: independent supplies do not create additional bench capacity. Concurrent repair and copying require genuinely compatible space/access supplied by the fixture. The selected bench is a fixture requirement, not a universal Alchemy-workbench requirement for copying.

For persistence, if schema16 histories already record the old kit-triggered copying pauses, preserve those historical transitions through the versioned replay policy. Apply corrected eligibility without rewriting earned work, paid supplies or earlier receipts.

content.text: One repair-claim interaction to settle while implementing: your target claim expressly excludes overlapping repairs, but use of a still-functional partially damaged kit during its repair is not specified. Proposed narrow completion: active physical repair makes that target unavailable for productive tool use; paused/AwaitingCheck retains the exclusive repair claim but does not by itself disable an otherwise functional target. Broken always disables. Research sharing a target kit pauses if its repair work actually starts; no automatic resume. Same plot station spill blocks repair too as ordinary productive use; fouling/miscalibration of the Alchemy kit alone do not prohibit the separate carpentry repair task. Alternatively require the claim to block all target use untilsettled. Please select consistent boundary; no need to invent handling/transfers.

items.text:
**Select the first policy: exclusive productive use during active repair, with the repair claim persisting independently during pause/AwaitingCheck.** Record this as a NEW narrow completion.

| Repair state | Target use |
|---|---|
| Scheduled, not working | Claim blocks another repair; otherwise functional, accessible target may be used. |
| Active physical repair | Target unavailable for other productive tool use. |
| Paused / AwaitingCheck | Claim still blocks another repair; no additional productive-use prohibition merely from that claim. |
| Broken | Functional benefits remain unavailable regardless of repair state. |

Apply these boundaries:

- Validate authority, prerequisites and access **before** starting repair. Then atomically pause conflicting research and acquire exclusive productive access. Scheduling or a rejected start must not pause research.
- Pausing repair releases active-use exclusivity, but does not automatically resume research. It creates no HP restoration, reassembly, movement or custody change; the target must actually remain usable.
- **Final-check clarification:** resolution requires exclusive access to the target for that atomic operation. An explicit AwaitingCheck resume pauses conflicting productive use after validation, then resolves the check. This adds no elapsed time, labor window or material charge. Ordinary eligible completion resolves while repair already holds access.
- Cancellation/completion releases the repair claim; interrupted research still requires explicit resume.

Your restriction interpretation is consistent, with one terminology correction: **fouling belongs to the station, not the Alchemy kit.**

- A spill blocks repair when repair actually uses that affected station. Merely sharing a plot is insufficient.
- The fouled-station restriction applies to manufacturing orders; it does not automatically prohibit this separate carpentry repair when physically feasible.
- Miscalibration of the Alchemy target does not prohibit repair using the separate valid Carpenter’s tools. Repair leaves that miscalibration intact.

Keep **repair-claim exclusivity**, **active productive-use exclusivity**, **physical usability** and **station restrictions** as separate predicates. That prevents either a paused claim becoming an unintended universal lock or an active repair allowing simultaneous incompatible work.
